pilots.purpose: Prove the Urban, Human/Crowd and Animation Kit foundations can work together without establishing Kenney's visual style as final Drift art.
technical_behavior_implemented: GLTFLoader.loadAsync via three/examples/jsm, one load per mount, no module-level GPU-resource cache (see disposal rationale)

SkeletonUtils.clone (three/examples/jsm/utils/SkeletonUtils.js) creates N independent skinned character instances from one loaded GLB — plain Object3D cloning would share bind skeletons across instances

one THREE.AnimationMixer per character instance; a per-character Map<clipName, AnimationAction> cache guarantees clipAction is never re-created for an already-used clip — deterministic switching without accumulation by construction, not by trusting three.js's own internal cache alone
idle -> walk -> interact-right cycle, 3.2s hold, 0.4s crossfade
City Kit background massing: one InstancedMesh per building form (2 forms), deterministic seeded placement (same hash() pattern as drift3dScatter.ts), one shared material per form
hybrid distance: N real skinned characters (base 3) + a silhouette-only InstancedMesh capsule crowd (base 24), both Quality-Tier-scaled
no React component per crowd/building instance
pilots.quality_tier_behavior: getDrift3DUrbanHumanCounts(tier) scales animatedCharacterCount, silhouetteCrowdCount and backgroundBuildingCount via the existing scaleDrift3DQualityCount, monotonic low<=medium<=high (unit-tested)
pilots.fallback_behavior: reducedMotion prop freezes mixer.update(0) and silhouette bob; pilot itself renders nothing when no-WebGL (handled at the shell level, see DriftKitLab.tsx)
pilots.disposal_result: on unmount: mixer.stopAllAction()+uncacheRoot per character, full geometry/material/texture traversal-dispose (disposeDrift3DKitObject3D) per character root, InstancedMesh geometry dispose + removal per building form, cached geometry/material Maps disposed and cleared, disposalCount incremented — implemented and type-checked; live confirmation blocked, see known limitation
known_limitations: live render, screenshots, FPS, draw-call/triangle counts, disposal-count-stays-bounded-across-switches all KNOWN_ENVIRONMENT_LIMITATION this session
prohibited_claims: Kenney's low-poly appearance is not final human or foreground architectural art; City Kit stays background/distant massing only

pilots.purpose: Prove the existing Vegetation Kit and a new background Vehicle/Traffic Kit path can coexist as reusable world infrastructure.
shared_services_reused: Drift3DScatterField/drift3dScatter.ts (existing Vegetation Kit, unmodified, mounted as-is)
new_infrastructure_this_lot: traffic path/wheel math in drift3dKitPilotConfig.ts (sampleDrift3DTrafficPath, getDrift3DTrafficLoopProgress, computeDrift3DWheelRotationDelta — all pure, unit-tested)
technical_behavior_implemented: one real sedan.glb load; named nodes resolved by exact string (body, wheel-front-left, wheel-front-right, wheel-back-left, wheel-back-right) — re-confirmed this lot via an independent standard-library-only glTF parser, matching DRIFT-IV-PRE-20's own recorded structure exactly
one InstancedMesh per named part (5 total), instances = Quality-Tier-scaled vehicle count, geometry/material shared across all vehicle instances
deterministic closed elliptical path (sampleDrift3DTrafficPath), staggered per-vehicle start offset so N vehicles distribute around the loop

wheel rotation = distance/radius (computeDrift3DWheelRotationDelta) accumulated from a nominal constant speed also used to derive the loop duration from the path's approximate circumference, so 'path speed' and 'wheel speed' are the same number
vehicle body orientation = path tangent heading (atan2), wheel world position = vehicle position + heading-rotated local wheel offset
no rigid-body/collision simulation, no interaction with the player's vehicle physics
Drift3DScatterField mounted completely unmodified — real reuse, not a rebuild
pilots.quality_tier_behavior: getDrift3DNatureMovementCounts(tier) scales trafficVehicleCount (monotonic, unit-tested) and exposes vegetationScatterScale (read from the same canonical profile Drift3DScatterField's own consumers would use, informational — the mounted Drift3DScatterField scales itself via its own existing, already-proven mechanism, not overridden here)
pilots.fallback_behavior: reducedMotion prop freezes elapsed-time accumulation and wheel-angle accumulation (vehicles hold their last position/pose)
pilots.disposal_result: on unmount: all 5 InstancedMeshes removed and their geometries disposed, cached geometry Map disposed+cleared, shared material (+its texture) disposed, disposalCount incremented — implemented and type-checked; live confirmation blocked, see known limitation

pilots.purpose: Prove three.js Water/Sky, the existing atmosphere/effects foundations and the accepted Poly Haven snow material can coexist in a reusable technical substrate.
new_infrastructure_this_lot: a small procedural water-normal CanvasTexture generator, matching the existing drift3dTextureFactory.ts procedural-canvas convention — avoids introducing a new third-party normal-map asset just to satisfy Water.js's required option
technical_behavior_implemented: direct `import { Water } from 'three/examples/jsm/objects/Water.js'` and `import { Sky } from 'three/examples/jsm/objects/Sky.js'` — no source copied, no new npm dependency, no second three.js version, no second renderer
one PlaneGeometry water mesh + one Sky mesh built once per mount
two bounded presets (calm-canal-seed, rough-open-water-seed) toggle distortionScale/waveSpeed/sunElevationDegrees on the existing Water/Sky material uniforms — no rebuild

snow_02 diffuse (sRGB)/normal-GL (linear)/roughness (linear) wired into a MeshStandardMaterial via the same TextureLoader + colorSpace/wrap convention drift3dTextureFactory.ts already uses for the 5 existing Poly Haven sets
reduced motion freezes water.material.uniforms.time
textureWidth/textureHeight for Water's reflection render target scaled via scaleDrift3DQualityDimension(reflectionResolutionScale)
pilots.quality_tier_behavior: getDrift3DWaterWeatherLightCapabilities(tier) exposes reflectionResolutionScale/renderProbeScale from the existing canonical profile, monotonic and capped at 1 on high (unit-tested)
pilots.fallback_behavior: reducedMotion prop stops the water time uniform from advancing (visually frozen surface); pilot itself renders nothing when no-WebGL
pilots.disposal_result: on unmount: water/sky/snow meshes removed from the scene graph; water geometry+material, procedural normal texture, sky geometry+material, snow geometry+material+3 textures all explicitly .dispose()d — implemented and type-checked. KNOWN UPSTREAM LIMITATION: Water.js's internal reflection WebGLRenderTarget is a private constructor-closure variable with no public accessor or dispose() method anywhere in three/examples/jsm/objects/Water.js (confirmed by reading the installed source) — this pilot cannot call .dispose() on a render target it was never given a reference to. This is a three.js addon limitation, not a gap in this pilot's own disposal code.
known_limitations: live render, screenshots, FPS, draw-call/triangle counts, disposal-count-stays-bounded-across-switches all KNOWN_ENVIRONMENT_LIMITATION this session

Water.js internal render-target disposal is architecturally unavailable via public API (see disposal_result) — real GPU-memory-growth-across-repeated-mounts could not be measured this session either way
prohibited_claims: does not implement Étééaooété or its erasure mechanic; does not complete the Water Kit; does not establish final ocean/weather/snow-line art; Water.js/Sky.js remain technical seeds only; no giant symbolic sun
